correctness.rationale: For nonsingular binary targets, the reduction lemma rigorously forces all nonnegative integer factors to be binary, allowing exact finite exhaustion. The support inequality proves atomicity of every four-one shear and all six six-one determinant-two matrices. Every singular binary target admits a zero-row/duplicate-row or zero-column/duplicate-column factorization. A standalone standard-library verifier enumerates all 512 binary targets, all 506^2 ordered nonunit binary factor pairs, all row/column double orbits and exact integer determinants. It constructs factorizations for each remaining target, obtains exactly 42 atoms and six units, and returns VERIFY_OK. The program is in the exact deliverable. No finite result is asserted beyond its scope.

originality.rationale: Direct theorem-to-theorem comparison with Bell et al. (2026), Baeth et al. (2021/2022), and Chen (2015) finds neither an exact 42-element census nor a complete binary order-three atom-orbit classification. The known elementary shear family is credited. The exceptional determinant-two cycle orbit and completeness are not entailed by the cited 2-by-2 algorithms, general partial families, or the upper-triangular subsemigroup theorem. Several targeted semantic and public-literature searches found no covering statement; their failure is not uniqueness proof, and a possible earlier finite census remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier isolated three-by-three zero-one prime-matrix census may be filed under incidence-matrix or nonnegative semigroup terminology.
The full supplementary data of all potentially relevant older articles were not exhaustively canvassed; semantic retrieval is not proof of absence.
Independent mathematical and bibliographic auditing is not performed.

value.rationale: A complete natural small-order boundary in the full multiplicative nonnegative-integer matrix monoid resolves the first nontrivial three-dimensional binary cutoff after published 2-by-2 theory. The six cyclic non-upper-triangular determinant-two atoms are qualitatively different from the 36 known elementary-shear associates; the theorem identifies exactly when this new obstruction arises and supplies explicit factorizations for the entire complement. The exact two-orbit classification and a reproducible comprehensive decision census support future atom searches and incidence-matrix factorability investigations.
